get.description: Hashes the stored signed copy as it is now and compares it with the hash anchored on-chain. The verdict is computed server-side. When the status is TAMPERED, the archived original (re-hashed against the chain) and the current file are both extracted and diffed: `tamper_report` lists the changed segments with page and bbox where the OCR engine reports layout. If that diff cannot be produced, `tamper_report_status` is UNAVAILABLE and the TAMPERED verdict still stands. A deleted file is FILE_MISSING, a tamper finding; VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE means storage or the chain could not be read. The chain is read first, so an anchored document is checked whatever its `lifecycle` says. Every check that reaches a verdict is kept for the integrity report. With `report=false` this is the quick check made when a document is opened: hashes only, no OCR and no `tamper_report`, and an AUTHENTIC or NOT_ANCHORED verdict is not kept.

post.summary: Repair a tampered document from the chain and its archive
post.description: Repairs everything found wrong, in one transaction: the lifecycle, the snapshot row, the file and the metadata. Offer it when the verdict's `needs_restore` and `permissions.can_restore` are both true. Every value comes from the chain and the archive, which is found from the on-chain hash, so an altered row can't block it. The archived original is re-hashed against the on-chain hash, then becomes the current signed copy; a tampered file is kept in /signed-copies and the restore is recorded in /history with both hashes and, in `changes`, every record value's old and new form. For a deleted file nothing is preserved, and `preserved_copy_id`, `previous_hash` and the history row's `from_hash` are null. `repaired` lists what was put back; `unrepaired` lists what needs a database backup. The on-chain records are unchanged. If nothing is wrong nothing changes and `restored` is false, so a retry is safe. `verification` is a fresh check of the result.

status.title: Status
status.description: AUTHENTIC — the stored file matches the chain; TAMPERED — it does not; FILE_MISSING — the stored file was deleted (a tamper finding; `current_hash` is null and there is no diff); SNAPSHOT_COMPROMISED — the file was changed or deleted and the stored original was altered too, so no trustworthy baseline exists to diff against; NOT_ANCHORED — the document was never finalized and the chain has no record of it; VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE — storage or the chain could not be read, or an anchor exists with no finalized state or frozen record to check it against, so integrity is unknown (not a tamper finding by itself)
